review: Three priors exist, two mine and one from another machine. I picked the target by reading what all three say they did NOT do, and they name the same corner: j62b1 does vector at one level and lists the J-level vector statement as open, jafb3 does scalar at J levels and lists the vector version as open, the third lists multi-component as unclassified. So I did the intersection: nonnegative matrix weights over finitely many levels. The proof is the block companion matrix plus entrywise domination by the nonnegative C(0), with Wielandt's equality case doing the classification - and I flag that Wielandt is ASSUMED, not re-proved, which makes the classification half conditional in all three treatments since the others lean on the same lemma in scalar or one-level form. Two things the vector case adds, both with exact witnesses: single-site entries are necessary and NOT sufficient (a two-component rule with single-site entries that mixes has every branch strictly inside the circle), and the transport velocity is rational not integral. Along the way I fixed three of my own errors: a symbol-assumption mismatch, expand_complex splitting lambda into re/im, and a reversed-polynomial index that rebuilt conj(P) instead of the reversal. The converse is not proved and the examples are all d=1.

The referee's correction to a failed attempt: a SINGLE NEGATIVE REAL weight on the level before last already gives the discrete wave equation with real records; unitary phases are not the weakest change. TASK: (a) the multi-level theorem: with nonnegative weights over finitely many earlier levels, no branch of the dispersion relation has |lambda(k)| = 1 on an open set (prove it, or find the exception); (b) classify the minimal signed rules that do propagate: theta_{t+1} = 2a P theta_t - theta_{t-1} and relatives: dispersion, stability region, the speed; (c) the question for the axiom: overlap weights are probabilities of records, so a negative weight is not a probability. What formation rule on AMPLITUDES (complex record amplitudes combined by a unitary local rule, probabilities by the squared modulus at readout) reproduces the signed recursion for the amplitude and what does it give for the record statistics? Work the smallest example exactly (two-component amplitude on the 1+1 event lattice: the unitary nearest-neighbour rule and its dispersion) and state what is kept and what is lost relative to the positive formation law (order-independence, the Green-function static kernel, reversibility). triage.note: Closes the corner all three prior attempts name as open: nonnegative MATRIX weights over FINITELY MANY levels. Branches are the block companion matrix's eigenvalues; nonnegativity gives entrywise |C(k)| <= C(0) and gain one gives rho(C(0)) = 1, so every branch has |lambda| <= 1, and Wielandt's equality case (ASSUMED, stated - the one imported theorem) forces single-displacement entries plus a diagonal phase conjugation, i.e. rigid transport. The vector case adds two things with exact witnesses: single-site entries are necessary and NOT sufficient (a two-component rule with single-site entries that mixes has every branch strictly inside the circle, certified by an exact resultant), and the transport velocity is rational not integral (theta_{t+1} = theta_{t-1}(x-1) has dispersion lambda^2 - e^{-ik}, branches +- e^{-ik/2}). A two-component two-level rigid rule has dispersion lambda^4 - 1 identically in k. Unimodular claims are verified symbolically in k; non-unimodular ones by resultant certificates over cyclotomic coefficients. The converse is not proved and all witnesses are d=1.
